material_findings.canon_label_hint: Research Progress - 2026-03-16 - Bridge-field behavior for `provider_attempt_ref`, `usage_event_ref`, and receipts
heading_hints: Research Progress - 2026-03-16 - Bridge-field behavior for `provider_attempt_ref`, `usage_event_ref`, and receipts
exact_items: start from `attempt_id`
follow `provider_attempt_ref` to provider/runtime trace and low-level execution evidence
follow `usage_event_ref` to canonical Usage/Ledger identity
follow receipt refs to Git/Actions/Docker/Kubernetes lineage
follow `artifact_id` / `linked_artifact_id` for renderable outputs and evidence objects
none of these bridge fields should become a replacement primary key
`provider_attempt_ref` does not replace `attempt_id`
`usage_event_ref` does not replace runtime identity
receipt refs do not replace artifact identity
Treat timestamp/run/thread fallback routing as compatibility behavior only when canonical bridge refs are absent.

material_findings.canon_label_hint: Research Progress - 2026-03-16 - Runtime-artifact envelope minimum contract
heading_hints: Research Progress - 2026-03-16 - Runtime-artifact envelope minimum contract
exact_items: the runtime-artifact envelope should be attempt-native by default.
`artifact_id` is the canonical identity of the renderable artifact object itself.
`logical_artifact_id` and `linked_artifact_id` are lineage/navigation helpers, not replacements for runtime identity.
`attempt_id` should be present whenever the artifact came from a concrete execution attempt.
if there is no concrete attempt, the envelope should still carry the strongest available runtime anchor.
`tool_llm_trace`
`validation_test`
`failed_attempts`
`before_after_snapshot`
